cohorts.label: 2-20h
cohorts.summary: Players navigate complex branching paths and timed choices where critical failures trigger permanent deaths.

claims.claim: The game features multiple branching paths and an extensive choice system where player decisions significantly impact character survival and story outcomes.

citations.review_text:
Detroit: Become Human is basically an interactive movie but the story pulled me in enough that I wanted to see what would happen next. We follow the stories of three androids and our choices can change their paths and the ending. The game looks great and the scenes are well acted and well made.
It is a game by the creators of Heavy Rain so just like in that game we can make choices that affect what happens next and how the other characters react. Something that seems small at first can become the most important choice in the game. The best way to play is to follow your heart and choose what feels right. Avoid guides and see where your choices take you. Then take a year or so off and play again to see if anything turns out differently. The game has lots of moral and ethical choices and sometimes none of them are good but the choice is yours. Good luck.

DBH is an amazing game. I've always been fascinated by choice-driven games, and this is arguably one of the best examples of the category. The sheer number of possible outcomes (approximately 85 endings) is honestly insane to me. What I appreciate most, is how much weight and agency the game gives to its decisions. Almost every choice feels consequential, and the options presented are almost never arbitrary. You're often given several plausible responses, each reflecting something you could reasonably think or do. It allows the experience to be considerably more immersive since most things would think of doing, you have the option to literally just do them in the game. Whether or not that has a negative effect is up to you though.

What makes this particularly effective is the uncertainty surrounding the consequences of your decisions. You never really know how much plot armor a character has, or whether a seemingly insignificant decision could eventually result in someone’s death. (I.e turning off Alice’s temperature controls) The possibility of losing characters you’ve grown attached to creates this palpable tension that makes even mundane interactions feel almost frightening. You genuinely just have no idea what could go wrong and that uncertainty makes the experience all the more engaging. There were so many times I regretted a decision, but given the fact that most choices are timed, you don't get much time to think about them. There were so many times that I would be audibly freaking out over something, like when I was trying to escape from that mansion where Luther originally worked at.

Kara's storyline is probably the best example of this though. As I progressively became attached to both her and Alice, their survival became something I needed to maintain. Knowing that a single slip up in my decision-making could determine whether they were captured, separated, or killed made their journey extremely stressful. a game way ahead of its time. great graphics and soundtrack. really good characters and plot. gameplay is mostly qte’s and choices, but that doesn’t take away from the game. if you’re going to buy this game, buy it on sale (this doesn’t mean full price isn’t worth it). there are so many possibilities in this game, but it’s short if you do one run only. I recommend doing a run with one choice and doing a run with the other choice. keep in mind if you miss certain qte’s in the story or make the wrong choices it’ll result in a character death.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Longer sessions highlight technical instability and awkward camera angles that hide environment details.

claims.claim: This cohort reports that the camera angles during gameplay are unhelpful, automatically shifting and causing players to miss clues or objects in rooms.

citations.review_text:
You know what they say, can't have shi…

 I first played this game a few years back, but with the increase of AI now, it was interesting to go back and 100% this game. This interactive decision-making story game is allegorical to the social and civil rights issues with ties to slavery and segregation in the real world, yet provides interesting plots and art style that makes you think quickly about your own morality. 

 A couple things I will say - The camera angles are not the most reliant throughout the whole gameplay, causing some things to be missed by being possibly unapproachable. The relationships between the characters seem a bit flimsy at times, as if the dynamics between them don't line up naturally. 

Overall, would recommend!

A very good choice-based game.

Story : I really enjoyed the storylines, and the acting was excellent. (Even though some parts were hit-or-miss, for example I think Marcus and North lacked chemistry). Frank and Connor are a top-notch duo, I couldn't get enough of them. Alice and Kara took me by surprise, there's some great elements and some "meh" elements in their story.

I particularly liked that depending on my choices, there was some true variation to how things end for each character.

Gameplay : I liked the exploring/discovering and the QTE's, but I do have one BIG annoyance which was the camera constantly swooping around in a direction that didn't suit me, or trying to snap back to a pre-determined angle in a way that made me miss a few things in the room I was exploring / trying to find clues in. I'm playing on keyboard/mouse, I don't need auto camera, for the love of god please stop trying to "assist" me.

Anyway, this being a story-based game it's hard to say anything more without spoiling the story. The artwork and music were good.

citations.review_text: The game is great story wise, but this shit isnt optimized at all

Great game with surprising variety of choices that actually drastically change the story. Story is corny AF but has a charm to it. Connor and Hank are the best parts.
It can crash though. For Nvidia, change the "Vulkan/OpenGL Present method" in nvidia app to "Prefer layered on DXGI swapchain"
